concepts.name: Panchamahavrata: The Five Great Vows of Jainism
key_dimensions: Distinction between Mahavrata (for monks) vs Anuvrata (for laypeople) — a classic UPSC trap
Comparison with Buddhist Panchashila: overlaps and critical differences (e.g., Brahmacharya and Aparigraha absent in Buddhist version)
Addition of Brahmacharya as the 5th vow by Mahavira vs Parshvanatha's four-fold path (Chaturyama)
How each vow philosophically connects to the core doctrine of Ahimsa

concepts.name: Ahimsa as the Supreme Principle in Jainism
key_dimensions: Scope of Ahimsa in Jainism vs Buddhism — Jainism extends it to microorganisms (Nigodas), making it more radical
Philosophical basis: all living beings possess Jiva (soul) capable of suffering
Practical implications: dietary restrictions, occupational choices, and why Jains avoided agriculture
Distinction between Sthavar Jiva (immobile, one-sensed) and Trasa Jiva (mobile, multi-sensed) — determines degree of harm

concepts.name: Anekantavada: Doctrine of Many-Sidedness (Non-Absolutism)
key_dimensions: Core philosophical meaning: reality is complex and cannot be expressed from a single viewpoint
Relationship with Syadvada and Nayavada — the three are interconnected doctrines, often confused in exams
Contrast with Buddhist Madhyamaka philosophy and Hindu Advaita — UPSC comparison trap
Political and ethical implications: tolerance, non-dogmatism; used in modern contexts

concepts.name: Syadvada: Theory of Conditional Predication (Saptabhangi)
key_dimensions: The seven-fold predication system (Syat asti, Syat nasti, Syat avaktavya, etc.) — logical structure
How Syadvada is the epistemological expression of Anekantavada
Criticism by other schools (Advaita Vedanta, Buddhism) — called self-contradictory or fence-sitting
Difference between Syadvada (logic/language) and Anekantavada (metaphysics) — a nuance UPSC tests

concepts.name: Nayavada: Doctrine of Partial Standpoints
key_dimensions: Definition: each Naya (standpoint) captures only a partial truth about reality
Seven Nayas listed in Jain texts — Naigama, Sangraha, Vyavahara, etc.
Relationship to Anekantavada and Syadvada: Nayavada is the analytical tool, Syadvada is the verbal expression
UPSC trap: distinguishing Nayavada from Syadvada and Anekantavada as three distinct but related concepts

concepts.name: Jiva and Ajiva: The Fundamental Ontological Categories
key_dimensions: Jiva (soul/consciousness) vs Ajiva (non-soul/matter) — the two primary categories of Jain metaphysics
Sub-categories of Ajiva: Pudgala, Dharma, Adharma, Akasha, Kala — often asked in Prelims
Comparison with Samkhya dualism (Purusha vs Prakriti): similarities and critical differences
Role of Jiva-Ajiva distinction in understanding bondage (Bandha) and liberation (Moksha)

concepts.name: Theory of Karma in Jainism
key_dimensions: Jain Karma as a physical/material substance (Karma Pudgala) that attaches to the soul — unlike Buddhist or Hindu views where Karma is intentional/moral
Eight types of Karma: Ghati (destructive, e.g., Jnanavarniya) and Aghati (non-destructive) — classification tested in Prelims
Mechanism: Asrava (influx) → Bandha (bondage) → Samvara (stoppage) → Nirjara (shedding) → Moksha
UPSC trap: Jain Karma is materialistic, not merely intentional — contrast with Buddhist Karma which is intention-based (Cetana)

concepts.name: Asrava, Samvara, and Nirjara: Process of Karmic Bondage and Liberation
key_dimensions: Asrava: influx of Karma through activities of mind, body, speech — five channels
Samvara: stoppage of Karma influx through ethical practices, meditation, vows
Nirjara: shedding of accumulated Karma through austerities (Tapas) — active vs passive Nirjara
How this process constitutes the Jain path to liberation — maps onto the Ratnatraya (Three Jewels)

concepts.name: Ratnatraya: The Three Jewels of Jainism
key_dimensions: Right Faith (Samyak Darshana), Right Knowledge (Samyak Jnana), Right Conduct (Samyak Charitra) — the triple path
Comparison with Buddhist Noble Eightfold Path and the concept of Prajna, Sila, Samadhi — overlap and distinction
Interdependence: all three must coexist; Right Faith without Right Conduct is insufficient — philosophical nuance
UPSC trap: Jainism's Ratnatraya vs Buddhism's Triratna (Buddha, Dhamma, Sangha) — same term, entirely different meaning

concepts.name: Parshvanatha's Chaturyama and Mahavira's Reformation
key_dimensions: Parshvanatha's four vows: Ahimsa, Satya, Asteya, Aparigraha — Mahavira added Brahmacharya as 5th
Significance: establishes continuity of Jain tradition before Mahavira — Jainism is not founded by Mahavira
UPSC trap: Mahavira as the 24th Tirthankara, not the founder — Rishabhadeva (Adinatha) is the first Tirthankara
Historical implication: Jainism predates the Vedic consolidation period, used to argue for its antiquity

concepts.name: Concept of Tirthankara and Mahavira's Place in Jain Tradition
key_dimensions: Definition: Tirthankara as ford-maker who creates a path across the ocean of worldly existence — not a creator god
24 Tirthankaras in the current cosmic cycle: Rishabhadeva (1st) to Mahavira (24th)
Mahavira's biographical details: born in Vaishali, attained Kaivalya under a Sal tree at Jrimbhikagrama, Nirvana at Pavapuri
UPSC trap: Mahavira's Nirvana vs Buddha's Nirvana — different locations, different philosophical meanings of Nirvana in each tradition

concepts.name: Kaivalya: The Jain Concept of Omniscience and Liberation
key_dimensions: Kaivalya = perfect knowledge/omniscience achieved upon total destruction of Ghati Karmas — not the same as Moksha
Distinction: Kaivalya (omniscience while living) vs Moksha (final liberation after death when Aghati Karmas also shed)
Comparison with Buddhist Nirvana: Buddhist Nirvana has no concept of omniscient soul; Jain Kaivalya involves an eternal, perfected Jiva
Jiva in liberated state (Siddha) — location, nature, attributes: a Prelims favorite

concepts.name: Jain Cosmology: Loka, Aloka, and the Nature of Universe
key_dimensions: Universe (Loka) is eternal, uncreated — no creator God (Ishvara) in Jainism; contrast with Hindu theism
Three realms: Urdhva Loka (heavens), Madhya Loka (human realm), Adho Loka (hells) — tested in Prelims
Concept of Kalachakra (time cycles): Utsarpini (ascending) and Avasarpini (descending) half-cycles
UPSC trap: Jainism rejects God as creator but accepts liberated souls (Siddhas) as objects of veneration — theistic vs non-theistic classification

concepts.name: Digambara vs Shvetambara: Schism and Doctrinal Differences
key_dimensions: Origin of schism: ~300 BCE, associated with Bhadrabahu (Digambara) vs Sthulabhadra (Shvetambara)
Key doctrinal differences: nudity as essential to liberation (Digambara) vs optional (Shvetambara); status of women achieving liberation
Textual differences: Digambaras reject the Agamas as authentic; Shvetambaras accept 45 Agamas
UPSC trap: Digambaras believe Mahavira never married; Shvetambaras say he did — factual trap in Prelims

concepts.name: Jain Ethics and Concept of Tapas (Austerity)
key_dimensions: Twelve forms of Tapas: six external (Bahya) and six internal (Abhyantara) — classification tested
Sallekhana/Santhara: voluntary fasting unto death — philosophical justification vs modern legal controversies (Rajasthan HC 2015 case)
Role of Tapas in shedding Karma (Nirjara) — connects ethics to metaphysics
Comparison with Buddhist Middle Path: Buddhism explicitly rejects extreme austerity that Jainism endorses — a critical contrast

concepts.name: Jain Theory of Knowledge (Pramana and Five Types of Jnana)
key_dimensions: Five types of knowledge: Mati, Shruta, Avadhi, Manahparyaya, Kevala — progression from limited to omniscient
First two (Mati and Shruta) are indirect (Paroksha); last three are direct (Pratyaksha) — a Prelims trap
Kevala Jnana = omniscience, achieved only by Tirthankaras and liberated beings
Comparison with Buddhist epistemology (Pratyaksha, Anumana, Agama) — Jainism's unique five-fold system

concepts.name: Jainism's Rejection of Vedic Authority and Caste System
key_dimensions: Mahavira's rejection of Vedas as infallible — positions Jainism as a Nastika/Shramanic tradition alongside Buddhism
Critique of caste: liberation open to all varnas, but Digambaras restrict full monasticism — internal contradiction
Socio-political implication: appeal to Vaishya community — explains Jain merchant community's historical prominence
Comparison with Buddhism's rejection of caste: both opposed Brahmanical hegemony but through different philosophical routes

concepts.name: Spread of Jainism: Patronage, Geography, and Decline
key_dimensions: Royal patronage: Chandragupta Maurya (Digambara tradition), Kharavela of Kalinga — political history link
Geographic spread: strong in Rajasthan, Gujarat, Karnataka (Gomateshwara/Bahubali statue at Shravanabelagola)
Why Jainism didn't spread beyond India unlike Buddhism: extreme ascetic demands limited popular appeal
UPSC trap: Chandragupta Maurya's alleged conversion to Jainism and death by Sallekhana — connects to Mauryan history

concepts.name: Jain Literature and Canonical Texts (Agamas)
key_dimensions: Shvetambara canon: 12 Angas, 12 Upangas, and other texts — Acharanga Sutra (oldest, contains Mahavira's biography) is most important
Language: Jain Agamas written in Ardhamagadhi Prakrit — not Sanskrit; significance for linguistic history
Digambara rejection of existing Agamas — they consider original teachings lost; rely on later texts like Tattvartha Sutra
Tattvartha Sutra by Umasvati: first systematic philosophical text of Jainism, accepted by both sects — UPSC frequently asks about it

concepts.name: Concept of Moksha in Jainism vs Buddhism: A Comparative Analysis
key_dimensions: Jain Moksha: individual eternal soul (Jiva) attains perfect isolation (Kaivalya) at top of universe — soul retains identity
Buddhist Nirvana: no permanent self (Anatman); liberation is extinguishing of desire and illusion — no eternal soul
Process difference: Jainism requires physical austerity + ethical conduct; Buddhism prescribes Middle Path with mental cultivation
UPSC trap: both traditions are non-theistic and reject Vedas, yet have fundamentally opposed views on the existence of soul — a favorite comparison question
